This efficiency is supported by a robust multi-year sales uptrend and recent quarter-on-quarter sales growth [E48, E49]. While the market currently prices in an earnings growth expectation of 10.5%, the base case assumption of 18.0% suggests that the stock’s potential is significantly undervalued by current sentiment [E38]. Nevertheless, the company’s 277% compounded profit growth over the last three years highlights a powerful long-term trajectory that outweighs recent volatility [E16].

The market price of ₹ 127 sits at 94% of the 52-week range [E5], yet momentum has plainly stalled with trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth contracting by -5% [E17]. Investors also receive zero cash return for taking on this heightened valuation, as the dividend yield stands at an entirely barren 0.00% [E4].
